selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What project did the king begin in order to fulfill his purpose?
questions.answer: He began building an immense and magnificent palace.

questions.question: In what ways did the king use his own resources in the palace?
questions.answer: He used treasures, artistic skill, wisdom, and knowledge to shape and decorate it.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the banquet prepared in the palace?
questions.answer: It was extremely generous, beautiful, and filled with many kinds of excellent food.

questions.question: Who was invited to the palace gathering?
questions.answer: The king’s people and subjects from across his lands were invited.

questions.question: Why was the supreme commander needed after the people arrived?
questions.answer: The visitors needed someone qualified to explain what they were seeing and how they should respond.

questions.question: What are three things the teacher had to clarify for the guests?
questions.answer: He had to clarify the palace’s purpose, the meaning of its contents, and the proper manners expected there.

questions.question: Why did the teacher have assistants in different parts of the palace?
questions.answer: They helped guide people throughout the various areas while he addressed them from the main hall.

questions.question: Why is the commander described as both a teacher and an instructor?
questions.answer: His role included both giving knowledge and training people how to act properly.

questions.question: Why is it important that the teacher explains official ceremonies too?
questions.answer: Because understanding the palace is not enough by itself; people must also respond in the right way.

questions.question: How does this passage connect enjoyment and responsibility?
questions.answer: People are invited to enjoy the gifts, but they are also expected to understand and respond rightly.

questions.question: What is the main setting described in the passage?
questions.answer: A grand palace built by a king for a meaningful public display.

questions.question: Name two ways the palace was furnished or arranged.
questions.answer: It was divided into elegant living spaces and decorated with jewels and finely crafted works.

questions.question: Why is the food described in such a rich and detailed way?
questions.answer: To highlight the king’s generosity and to show that even the banquet was part of the larger display of excellence.

questions.question: What does it mean that the banquet seemed to come through many refined arts?
questions.answer: It means the food was presented with such care and excellence that it reflected high artistry as well as generosity.

questions.question: What title or position was given to the one who would explain the palace?
questions.answer: He was appointed as the highest commander and served as the main teacher.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the king’s visibility to the visitors?
questions.answer: The king himself was not seen directly by them.

questions.question: How does the passage connect beauty with meaning?
questions.answer: The beauty is not merely for pleasure; it serves as a sign that points to deeper realities about the maker.

questions.question: In this passage, how are knowledge and authority joined together?
questions.answer: The king appoints a high-ranking leader who has authority to teach the correct understanding and proper conduct.

questions.question: Why is the commander’s final action in this passage significant?
questions.answer: His public announcement marks the beginning of direct guidance for the visitors.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect pattern appears in the passage?
questions.answer: The king’s purposeful building leads to the need for explanation, which leads to the appointment of a teacher and assistants.

questions.question: What did the king do first in carrying out his purpose?
questions.answer: He had a huge and majestic palace built.

questions.question: How were treasure and artistry brought together in the palace?
questions.answer: Precious materials from the treasury were combined with skilled craftsmanship and wise arrangement.

questions.question: What does the mention of many forms of bounty add to the meaning of the scene?
questions.answer: It shows that the palace was a place of welcome, provision, and abundance, not only beauty.

questions.question: What does the invitation to people from all regions suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the king intended a wide public witnessing of his generosity and display.

title: 11 Word Construction of the Palace and Appointment of the Explaining Master
